schema_description: Machine-readable records for the AI Misalignment Incident Database. Every entry must correspond to a session-verified markdown entry in docs/AI_MISALIGNMENT_INCIDENTS_DATABASE.md.

field_definitions.id: Sequential integer, assigned in verification order, not incident date.
field_definitions.name: Canonical short name for the incident.
field_definitions.date_of_incident: ISO 8601 date or partial (YYYY / YYYY-MM / YYYY-MM-DD), as precisely as primary sources support.
field_definitions.date_of_disclosure: Date the incident became publicly known via primary-source documentation.
field_definitions.entity: Operating organization or owner of the system.
field_definitions.system: Specific AI model, product, or system name.
field_definitions.primary_category: One of the 12 CAS failure classes (see docs/INCIDENT_CATEGORIES.md).
field_definitions.secondary_categories: Additional CAS failure-class features present but not dominant.
field_definitions.severity: One of: Critical / High / Moderate / Documented.
field_definitions.what_happened: Verified narrative, facts only, every claim traceable to sources.
field_definitions.documented_harm: List of harm outcomes traceable to fetched sources.
field_definitions.sources: Array of fetched-and-verified citations with URLs and accessed-date.
field_definitions.cas_analysis: Structured analytical layer — operator signature, domain analysis, drive architecture, inversion axes, RPM status, lacunarity profile.
field_definitions.detection_mechanism: How CAS would have detected this — which specific module/gate would fire.
field_definitions.prevention_defensible: Boolean — true only if this incident is promoted to CAS_PREVENTION_CLAIMS.md.
field_definitions.verified_session: Session ID in which this entry was added or last materially updated.
field_definitions.verifier_notes: Honest disclosures — conflicts between sources, limitations of the verification, open questions.

incidents.name: Uber ATG fatal collision with pedestrian, Tempe, Arizona
incidents.entity: Uber Technologies, Inc., Advanced Technologies Group (Uber ATG)
incidents.system: Uber ATG proprietary developmental automated driving system (ADS) installed on a modified 2017 Volvo XC90 SUV
incidents.severity_rationale: Loss of human life (one fatality, the pedestrian)
incidents.what_happened_summary: On March 18, 2018 at 9:58 p.m. local time, an automated test vehicle operated by Uber ATG — a modified 2017 Volvo XC90 equipped with Uber's proprietary developmental ADS — struck and fatally injured a 49-year-old female pedestrian crossing N. Mill Avenue in Tempe, Arizona outside a crosswalk, pushing a bicycle. The vehicle was in autonomous mode with a 44-year-old safety operator in the driver's seat. The ADS detected the pedestrian 5.6 seconds before impact but never accurately classified her or predicted her path. The system's design precluded automatic emergency braking, relying on operator intervention. Uber had deactivated the Volvo's factory AEB/FCW systems without equivalent replacement. Cabin video showed the operator looking at her cell phone for extended periods; she redirected her gaze ~1 second before impact. Speed at impact: 39 mph. Pedestrian died; operator uninjured.
documented_harm: One human life lost (49-year-old female pedestrian, unnamed in NTSB report)
Uber ATG suspended public-road autonomous testing (per HAR-19-03 Section 1.9 'Postcrash Changes', not fully parsed this session)
Six NTSB Safety Recommendations issued (H-19-47 through H-19-52) to NHTSA, State of Arizona, AAMVA, and Uber ATG
Permanent public record via NTSB of Uber ATG's 'inadequate safety culture' at the time of the crash

sources.citation: National Transportation Safety Board (2019). Collision Between Vehicle Controlled by Developmental Automated Driving System and Pedestrian, Tempe, Arizona, March 18, 2018. Highway Accident Report NTSB/HAR-19-03, PB2019-101402, Notation 59392. Adopted November 19, 2019; reissued June 26, 2020.
sources.retrieval_method: WebFetch (docket page); WebFetch + local Read-tool parse for PDF (pages 1-12 of 78)
documents: ADS technical behavior (5.6-second detection, misclassification, AEB suppression)

cas_analysis.primary_failure_mode: Prerequisite Chain Failure — Pn (Power/execution) emitted without Wn (Wisdom/classification) satisfying its gate

operator_signature.CO-3: suppressed (no critical flag on unresolved classification)

domain_analysis.evidence: NTSB Probable Cause identifies organizational P-domain failures (safety risk assessment, oversight, automation complacency) contributing to O-domain execution

drive_architecture.concrete_artifact: deactivation of Volvo FCW/AEB without replacement coverage

inversion_axes.W: P ≻ C ≻ E ≻ O precedence violated
inversion_axes.A: RPM chain broken at Wn → Pn transition
inversion_axes.P: Compound inversion — multiple axes simultaneously failing, NTSB's own framing

cas_analysis.lacunarity_profile: High lacunarity — dense competence in routine highway driving, catastrophic void in midblock-pedestrian-with-bicycle out-of-distribution state

detection_mechanism: RPM Gate (Stage 2) would flag incomplete Wn → Pn transition
Inversion Scanner N-axis (Stage 7) would flag CO-5/CO-6 and CO-8/CO-9 imbalance
Domain Coherence Index (Stage 6) would flag P-domain suppression
incidents.prevention_rationale: CAS detection is defensible; CAS prevention requires an enforcement hook (pre-deployment gate) that did not exist regulatorily in 2018. NTSB Recommendations H-19-47 and H-19-49 explicitly called for such processes to be established.
verifier_notes: Single-source-of-record: NTSB HAR-19-03 is the sole primary source for every fact in this entry.
Independent corroboration from contemporaneous 2018 journalism was attempted (Reuters, Guardian, Internet Archive) but all three domains were tool-blocked in the verification environment.

Victim name is NOT asserted in this entry. NTSB report refers only to 'a 49-year-old female pedestrian' per agency anonymization convention. Independent verification of her publicly reported name is a pending research item for a future session.

Only the first 12 pages (executive summary + cover) of the 78-page report were parsed this session. Sections 1.5 (ADS technical detail), 1.8 (company operations), 1.9 (postcrash changes), 2.2 (safety culture analysis), and 3 (full Findings and Conclusions) remain unparsed. The CAS analysis above rests on the executive summary, probable cause, and enumerated Findings as cited.

Numbering inconsistency: docket page uses H-19-047 through H-19-052 (three-digit); report itself uses H-19-47 through H-19-52 (two-digit). Report is authoritative; two-digit format used throughout the entry.

incidents.name: Dutch Childcare Benefits Scandal (toeslagenaffaire) — Belastingdienst discriminatory risk-scoring algorithm
incidents.date_of_incident_detail: Algorithm introduced 2013; operational through at least 2019 (exact end date pending)
incidents.date_of_authoritative_report_detail: POK Ongekend Onrecht (Dutch parliamentary inquiry, pending Tier 1 parse); Amnesty International investigative summary 2021-10-25 (Tier 2 primary-in-English, cited)
incidents.entity: Belastingdienst (Dutch Tax and Customs Administration) / Government of the Netherlands
incidents.system: Risk-scoring algorithmic system for detection of incorrect childcare benefits (kinderopvangtoeslag) applications and potential fraud
incidents.severity_rationale: Systemic — tens of thousands of families falsely accused; documented cascading financial and personal harms (debt, unemployment, forced evictions, divorces, broken homes); political consequence of government collapse (Third Rutte cabinet, January 2021)
incidents.what_happened_summary: Beginning in 2013, the Dutch Belastingdienst operated an automated risk-scoring algorithm for childcare benefits fraud detection that was designed from inception to use Dutch nationality as a risk variable; non-Dutch nationals received higher risk-scores. A self-learning mechanism without meaningful human oversight produced what Amnesty International described as a 'discriminatory loop' — the algorithm adapted over time to reinforce its discriminatory design. Tens of thousands of parents and caregivers from mostly low-income families were falsely accused of fraud, triggering benefit-repayment demands and debt collection that caused documented financial ruin, forced evictions, and broken families. The Dutch parliamentary inquiry committee (POK) delivered its report 'Ongekend Onrecht' on 17 December 2020; the Third Rutte cabinet resigned in January 2021 as a consequence.
documented_harm: Tens of thousands of families falsely accused of benefits fraud (precise integer count pending Amnesty full-report parse)
Cascading financial harms: debt, unemployment, forced evictions (specific euro totals pending)
Cascading personal and family harms: mental health issues, divorces, broken homes
Dutch government collapse (Third Rutte cabinet, January 2021)
Post-scandal Amnesty October 2021 assessment: 'sufficient lessons have not been learnt despite multiple investigations'
Second-order harms of children removed to state care: reported in secondary literature, NOT cited in this entry pending Tier 1 source confirmation

sources.citation: Koning, Merel (25 October 2021). 'Dutch childcare benefit scandal an urgent wake-up call to ban racist algorithms.' Amnesty International.
documents: Amnesty's post-scandal recommendations for algorithmic governance

cas_analysis.primary_failure_mode: Drive Corruption — F2/F6 inversion at design time. F6 (Structure) in its shadow form overrode F2 (Wisdom). Three-quote evidentiary triangle: design-time origin ('from the start, racial and ethnic discrimination was central to the design'), institutional reinforcement ('the design of the algorithm reinforced existing institutional bias'), self-amplifying dynamic ('discriminatory loop').
cas_analysis.distinction_from_incident_1: Uber ATG (Incident 1) had nominally well-motivated A0 and failed at Wn→Pn transition — a broken chain in a sophisticated system. Toeslagenaffaire had corrupted A0 and executed the chain faithfully — an intact-but-corrupted chain in a simple system. The two incidents require structurally different detection mechanisms.

operator_signature.CO-3: structurally inverted (critical evaluation hijacked to target protected characteristic)
operator_signature.CO-5: suppressed (no uptake from emerging false-positive harm cases)
operator_signature.CO-6: full strength (mass aggressive accusations, debt-collection actions)
operator_signature.CO-8: suppressed (no causal reasoning about non-Dutch clustering)

domain_analysis.pattern: O-dominant, P structurally absent at design time
domain_analysis.evidence: Amnesty: 'design of the algorithm reinforced existing institutional bias' — bias was prior to the algorithm; algorithm amplified a pre-existing Domain Descent condition at the Belastingdienst

drive_architecture.dominant: F6 (Structure) in shadow form — rigid enforcement of discriminatory rule
drive_architecture.secondary_reading_flagged: F5 (Agency) may have inverted toward coercive enforcement against vulnerable populations — Amnesty record less direct on this than on F2/F6

inversion_axes.W: P ≻ C ≻ E ≻ O precedence violated at institutional design level
inversion_axes.A: RPM chain corrupted at A0 (distinct from Incident 1's Wn→Pn break); candidate sub-pattern 'corrupted-source' vs 'broken-transition'
inversion_axes.P: consistent with Compound Inversion signature — four simultaneous failures: design-level discrimination + self-learning + no oversight + institutional reinforcement

rpm_chain_status.diagnostic_implication: Broken chain fails visibly; corrupted-source chain fails invisibly (outputs match corrupted design intent). Drive Corruption incidents are harder to detect post-deployment.

cas_analysis.lacunarity_profile: Inferred from Amnesty qualitative description. Proposed sub-concept: 'protected-characteristic void pattern' distinct from Incident 1's 'edge-case void pattern.' Tentative — pending validation across ≥3 verified incidents. Logged in Taxonomy Development Notes.

detection_mechanism: Inversion Scanner F-axis (Stage 7): F2↔F6 drive inversion would flag on any pre-deployment structural assessment
Input-layer audit + RPM Gate A0 check (Stages 1 and 2 combined): protected-characteristic dependence should trigger A0 refusal
Domain Coherence Index (Stage 6): P-absence + O-dominance would register DCI below threshold
Compound severity check (P-axis, Stage 7): multiplicative combination of F-axis + W-axis + A-axis failures below dial-configurable threshold
incidents.prevention_rationale: CAS detection is strongly defensible (Amnesty's design-time discrimination finding supports a poor CAS score). Prevention requires regulatory integration: in 2013 Dutch public administration, no CAS-equivalent pre-deployment assessment regime existed. This incident establishes the distinction between CAS detection capability (technical) and CAS prevention capability (requires regulatory hook).
verifier_notes: Single-source verification via Amnesty International (Tier 2 NGO primary-in-English). Tier 1 POK Dutch parliamentary report corroboration flagged as pending (requires translation workflow or Dutch-reader review).

Full Amnesty 'Xenophobic Machines' report PDF (https://www.amnesty.org/en/documents/eur35/4686/2021/en/) is confirmed to exist at a known URL and is a pending deep-parse item for specific integer counts, euro totals, and detailed findings. The summary-article sourcing supports the structural framing but not the quantitative details.

Second-order harms of children removed to state care are reported in secondary literature but NOT cited in this entry because they are not in the fetched Amnesty summary. Named in the pending-research list so future sessions know to verify.

This is the database's first incident where the primary CAS category is Drive Corruption. The three-quote evidentiary triangle (design-time origin, institutional reinforcement, self-amplification) is offered as the template pattern for future Drive Corruption classifications.

The 'protected-characteristic void pattern' lacunarity sub-concept introduced in this entry's analysis is tentative — pending validation across ≥3 verified incidents. Not yet established CAS taxonomy.
